topic: empirical reply-to-proposition alignment in email and dialogue, focusing on partial replies, multiple questions, unanswered questions, and multi-proposition antecedents
executive_summary: The corpus establishes strong conceptual and transfer-method foundations for proposition-level reference and response scope, but it does not directly solve the target workplace problem. Abstract and discourse-deictic reference can target propositions, events, facts, utterances, and composite discourse objects, and antecedent selection is empirically difficult even in dialogue benchmarks [doi-10-1162-coli-a-00327, doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-778]. Formal work also supports partial answerhood and multiple simultaneously unresolved questions [doi-10-3765-sp-5-6, doi-10-1007-bf00351935]. However, none of the 13 papers empirically evaluates whether a workplace reply answers, approves, rejects, or clarifies one exact proposition while leaving neighboring propositions unresolved. Multi-proposition antecedents are theoretically plausible, but direct response-scope evidence is absent [manual-8b8a394daa]. Consequently, all five inherited gaps remain open. The strongest immediate path is an engineering benchmark with proposition-level gold targets, explicit partial and unresolved states, multiple antecedents, and conservative abstention.
themes: Propositional and discourse reference is distinct from ordinary entity coreference: antecedents may denote events, propositions, facts, situations, utterances, or speech acts [doi-10-1162-coli-a-00327, doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-778].

Exact antecedent selection is a major difficulty, and errors often arise from candidate generation, antecedent boundaries, parsing, or insufficient context rather than only from anaphor detection [1706.02256, doi-10-18653-v1-2021-naacl-main-329, doi-10-18653-v1-p17-1009].

Question semantics and QUD theory distinguish complete resolution from partial contribution, supporting the idea that one reply can advance a question without resolving all outstanding issues [doi-10-1007-bf00351935, doi-10-3765-sp-5-6].

Antecedent locality is useful but domain-dependent: discourse-deictic dialogue antecedents are often very local, whereas event reference can cross substantially longer distances [doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-778, manual-555fa5b6e8].

Rigid linguistic or structural constraints can improve precision for some constructions but exclude valid cases elsewhere; useful constraints should therefore be defeasible rather than absolute [doi-10-3115-v1-d14-1056, 1706.02256].

Composite antecedents are linguistically plausible: several propositions can form one coherent abstract discourse referent, and split-antecedent work independently demonstrates the computational need to represent more than one antecedent [manual-8b8a394daa, doi-10-18653-v1-2021-naacl-main-329].

The available empirical benchmarks are mostly dialogue, news, or general anaphora resources rather than authentic workplace email or enterprise chat [doi-10-18653-v1-2021-codi-sharedtask-1, doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-778, manual-555fa5b6e8].

findings.statement: A valid Topic 04 representation must allow antecedents that are propositions, events, facts, situations, utterances, or speech acts rather than assuming that every reference target is a nominal entity.

Exact antecedent boundaries should be treated as uncertain data rather than automatically assumed to be a whole message or whole utterance, because non-nominal antecedent spans are difficult to delimit and may be clausal, discontinuous, or multi-sentence.

Antecedent selection is itself a central empirical bottleneck: dialogue discourse-deixis performance improved primarily through better linking rather than better anaphor recognition, while split-antecedent resolution also showed large losses before final resolution because valid candidates were filtered or missed.

Partial answerhood is theoretically well motivated: an assertion can be relevant by providing only a partial answer to the current Question Under Discussion, so a response should not automatically close every question in its surrounding message.

The corpus provides no direct empirical method for determining which of several workplace questions was answered and which remain unanswered; the question-semantics papers supply formal structure but not workplace alignment benchmarks.

Composite proposition-level antecedents are plausible and should be representable: a coherent group of propositions can form a summed abstract discourse referent, while computational split-antecedent research shows that forcing a single antecedent can be structurally inadequate.

evidence.section: Proposed resolution procedure and discourse-topic analysis

findings.statement: Recency is a useful antecedent prior but cannot safely be a universal rule: more than 90 percent of discourse-deictic antecedents in one dialogue evaluation were within four utterances, whereas event-reference studies document materially longer-distance antecedents and weak performance for simple most-recent heuristics.

Hard syntactic restrictions are risky for response-scope resolution because syntactic cues help some tightly constrained constructions but hurt broader or more variable cases; lexical, syntactic, semantic, and discourse signals should be combined as defeasible evidence.

Joint modeling can exploit dependencies between detection and linking, but it is not uniformly beneficial: joint event modeling improved event coreference and anaphoricity, whereas joint split-antecedent training did not outperform the pre-trained alternative on the broader anaphora system.

No paper in the corpus directly validates proposition-level agreement, rejection, approval, clarification, or commitment scope in authentic workplace email or enterprise chat, so transfer evidence cannot establish msgloom's production-domain correctness.

contradictions.topic: How strongly antecedent search should be constrained by recency
contradictions.note: Dialogue discourse deixis strongly favors recent antecedents and benefits from a recency window, whereas event-reference work finds longer-distance links and poor performance from a simple most-recent-verb heuristic. This is a domain/task tension rather than a direct experimental contradiction, and it argues against imposing one fixed search window on workplace communication.

Shell-noun family syntax can help tightly constrained nouns, but strict constraints reduce accuracy for versatile nouns; likewise, explicit syntactic information helps one shell-noun setting yet can hurt unrestricted abstract-anaphora ranking. The combined evidence favors defeasible syntax rather than hard exclusion rules.

contradictions.topic: Whether joint training improves linked subtasks
contradictions.note: Joint event-trigger, anaphoricity, and coreference modeling improves all three event tasks, while joint split-antecedent training does not improve the ordinary anaphora components and is weaker overall than the pre-trained variant. Benefits from joint optimization are therefore architecture- and task-dependent.

contradictions.topic: Whether one contiguous textual span is an adequate antecedent representation
contradictions.note: The dialogue resolver operationalizes antecedents as whole utterances for tractability, while the survey and theoretical work explicitly identify clausal, discontinuous, multi-sentence, and composite abstract antecedents. The difference is an implementation simplification versus broader linguistic coverage, not evidence that whole-utterance targets are semantically sufficient.

gaps.description: Direct empirical evidence is still missing for proposition-level agreement, rejection, approval, clarification, and answer scope in authentic workplace email or enterprise chat, especially cases where one short response applies to only part of a preceding message.
gaps.suggested_query: "reply scope" email dialogue proposition agreement approval rejection workplace communication

gaps.description: The corpus still does not establish a validated annotation and evaluation scheme for mapping workplace responses to exact proposition or span targets while representing exact, partial, ambiguous, unsupported, discontinuous, and potentially multiple antecedents.

Direct evidence remains insufficient for aligning replies to one or more questions when a preceding workplace message contains multiple questions, requests, or alternatives, including detection of questions that remain unanswered.
gaps.suggested_query: "question answer alignment" dialogue "multiple questions" partial answer unanswered questions

gaps.description: It remains open whether and how a workplace response should be modeled as targeting a composite or multi-proposition antecedent. The corpus supports composite abstract discourse referents theoretically and multi-antecedent entity reference analogically, but provides no direct evaluation of multi-proposition reply scope in work communication.
gaps.suggested_query: "multi-antecedent" propositional anaphora dialogue composite discourse referent reply

gaps.description: The appropriate abstention, ambiguity, and missing-antecedent policy for msgloom remains unvalidated. The relative cost of an over-broad approval or commitment link versus leaving a link unresolved requires an explicit product-risk cost model and dedicated benchmark.

actionable_insights: Represent response scope as a relation from a response span to one or more proposition/span targets, not as a whole-message relation; allow clause-level, discontinuous, and composite targets [doi-10-1162-coli-a-00327, manual-8b8a394daa].

Maintain per-proposition state for multi-question messages so that one answered proposition can close independently while neighboring questions remain open; QUD theory supports partial rather than all-or-nothing answerhood [doi-10-3765-sp-5-6].

Separate candidate generation from relation classification and evaluate both, because upstream candidate filtering can remove valid antecedents before semantic resolution begins [doi-10-18653-v1-2021-naacl-main-329, doi-10-18653-v1-p17-1009].

Use recency as a weighted prior, not a hard cutoff. A local window is highly effective in some dialogue data but incompatible with documented longer-range event reference [doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-778, manual-555fa5b6e8].

Treat syntax, lexical cues, discourse structure, and rhetorical coherence as defeasible evidence. Do not let one syntactic pattern eliminate a semantically plausible target without additional evidence [doi-10-3115-v1-d14-1056, 1706.02256, manual-8b8a394daa].

Design gold annotations to permit zero, one, or multiple antecedent propositions and explicit labels for exact, partial, ambiguous, unsupported, and missing-context cases; the need for multiple and non-contiguous antecedents is supported by abstract- and split-antecedent research [doi-10-1162-coli-a-00327, doi-10-18653-v1-2021-naacl-main-329].

Score over-broad links separately from missed links. For msgloom, a false broad approval can incorrectly change downstream work state, so evaluation should expose this error class rather than hide it inside aggregate coreference F1 [doi-10-18653-v1-2021-codi-sharedtask-1, doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-778].

Keep unsupported or missing antecedents unresolved and hand missing-context cases to Topic 07 rather than forcing a nearest-candidate decision; poor proximity heuristics and large candidate spaces show why forced linking is unsafe [manual-5c0971730d, manual-555fa5b6e8].
confidence_summary: Confidence is HIGH that proposition/event/discourse antecedents require treatment beyond entity coreference, that antecedent selection and boundary identification are difficult, that partial answerhood is a legitimate discourse relation, and that hard single-candidate or whole-message assumptions are unsafe [doi-10-1162-coli-a-00327, doi-10-3765-sp-5-6, doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-778]. Confidence is MEDIUM for transferring composite-antecedent mechanisms to workplace reply scope because the supporting evidence is theoretical or analogical rather than direct [manual-8b8a394daa, doi-10-18653-v1-2021-naacl-main-329]. Confidence is LOW for any claim about production accuracy on authentic workplace email or enterprise chat because no included empirical study directly evaluates that target domain.
limitations: The corpus contains no direct empirical benchmark for proposition-level reply scope in authentic workplace email or enterprise chat; dialogue and news findings are transfer evidence only [doi-10-18653-v1-2021-codi-sharedtask-1, manual-555fa5b6e8].

The two central question-theoretic sources are formal semantic/pragmatic analyses rather than quantitative studies of observed multi-question reply alignment [doi-10-1007-bf00351935, doi-10-3765-sp-5-6].
One source on question resolution was available only through its abstract, limiting assessment of its detailed claims and formal scope [doi-10-1007-bf00983299].
The strongest composite-proposition evidence is qualitative and explicitly hypothetical rather than experimentally validated [manual-8b8a394daa].

Existing discourse-deixis benchmarks commonly simplify antecedent representation and do not directly evaluate exact sub-utterance response scope or business-state consequences [doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-778].

Several empirical datasets are small, sparse for difficult phenomena, or limited to specific genres, weakening conclusions about rare multi-antecedent and ambiguous cases [1706.02256, doi-10-18653-v1-2021-naacl-main-329].

The papers use heterogeneous tasks and metrics, so reported numerical performance is not directly comparable across abstract anaphora, discourse deixis, event coreference, and split-antecedent resolution [doi-10-1162-coli-a-00327].

gap_status.note: No included paper directly evaluates proposition-level agreement, rejection, approval, clarification, or answer scope in authentic workplace email or enterprise chat. Dialogue discourse-deixis work resolves abstract references but does not establish the semantic scope of workplace approvals or commitments.

The corpus supplies useful ingredients for an annotation design, including difficult span boundaries, discontinuous antecedents, multiple antecedents, gold-versus-predicted candidate evaluation, and partial answerhood, but no paper validates the complete workplace annotation/evaluation scheme required by msgloom.

Formal question semantics and QUD theory establish multiple questions, answer propositions, subquestions, and partial answers, but the corpus does not empirically align real replies to individual questions in multi-question workplace messages or measure unanswered-question detection.

Composite abstract referents are directly motivated theoretically, and split-antecedent computational work demonstrates multi-source reference, but no included study evaluates a workplace response whose semantic scope is a set or structured combination of preceding propositions.

No paper supplies the product-specific cost model needed to choose between over-broad linking, ambiguity, abstention, and unresolved missing-context states. Existing work shows that candidate selection is fallible but does not determine msgloom's acceptable risk tradeoff.
